demand: Inferred from the workflow and domain evidence; no verified request for this new tool.

100 fixed-seed graphs checked against exhaustive edge-state path enumeration, incoming-state counterexample, unreachable/identity route, zero cycle, invalid turns and negative-cost rejection.

discovery: Public searchable README/topics and reproducible tiny examples; no outreach, adoption or growth claim.
mutual_distinction: Nullable query predicates, dependency timing, token synchronization, road turn feasibility and finite-language inclusion have separate users and contracts. Shared packaging is infrastructure.
originality: Original code and invented fixtures, AI-assisted. No third-party implementation or prose copied; standard algorithms reimplemented.
user: Routing developers reproducing a turn-restriction bug on a small extracted directed graph.
pain: Keeping only the cheapest arrival at a junction can discard the incoming edge needed to take a legal next turn.
capability: Find minimum integer-cost routes over incoming-edge states with exact forbidden consecutive-edge pairs and compare an unrestricted baseline.
expected: Invented example takes ad,db,bc at cost4 instead of the blocked cost2 ab,bc route. A legal zero-cost loop can change the incoming edge and permit an exit.
limits: Normalized directed graph only; at most200 nodes/1000 edges/5000 distinct forbidden pairs; edge costs0..10^9. Pair IDs must refer to consecutive edges. No OSM/coordinates/geocoding, multi-edge/conditional/only-turn restrictions, travel-time prediction, turn penalties or vehicle safety instructions. All unlisted pairs including U-turns are allowed. Zero-cost loops are permitted. Ties deterministic for fixed IDs; no claim of globally lexicographically smallest route. Unreachable is a finding, not malformed input.
distinct: gpx-dwell-report analyzes recorded motion, redirect-graph checks web redirects and capacity-cut-report solves allocation flow. This is a route feasibility/cost witness for incoming-edge restrictions, not a map service.
checks: 100 fixed-seed graphs checked against exhaustive edge-state path enumeration, incoming-state counterexample, unreachable/identity route, zero cycle, invalid turns and negative-cost rejection.
